MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  APRIL 18, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  6:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Orders N-25-20
and N-29-20 and fully teleconferenced from various locations during the coronavirus
disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Hill called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Kraig Hill, Vice Chair Dennis Robert Smith, and Commissioners
  Jeffrey Jennings, John Mazza, and Mark Wetton

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Assistant City Attorney; Richard Mollica, Planning
  Director; Adrian Fernandez, Assistant Planning Director; Philip Coronel, Assistant
  Planner; Jessica Thompson, Senior Planner; Lauren Doyel, Coastal Engineer and
  Geotechnical Reviewer; and Rebecca Evans, Recording Secretary

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Wetton seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda as recommended by staff.

  The question was called and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on April 8, 2022. The amended agenda was posted on April 13, 2022.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS
  None.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of April 18, 2022

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Olivia Irion petitioned for the installation of guardrails along both Kanan Dume
  and Malibu Canyon Roads to prevent vehicular tragedies such as last week’s
  fatality.

  Jo Drummond stated that the Planning Department had not applied policy evenly
  when addressing Woolsey Fire rebuilds and second exemptions, which caused
  rapid development of excessively large homes. She added that the first exemption
  plus ten percent should be completed with a certificate of occupancy prior to
  processing a second exemption. She stated an intent to follow up with the
  California Coastal Commission regarding her concerns.

  John Johanessen asked if anything had been done to get the Malibu Film Society
  operating again within Malibu and questioned if Planning Director Mollica was
  unaware of the Film Society’s events and if the Planning Commissioners
  supported the Malibu Film Society.

  Howard Rudzki reminded the public and Commissioners that the Planning
  Department is significantly short-staffed, down four to five people, and has been
  getting a great deal done despite that. He commended Planning Director Mollica
  and his staff on their efforts.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION I STAFF COMMENTS

  Commissioner Mazza noted that Planning Director Mollica’s presentation on
  staffing had been scheduled for the City Council and the City Council will
  provide direction on priorities for staff time during the budget meeting and
  allocate funding. He added that those who wish to see staffing increased for
  Planning should submit correspondence to the City Council prior to their budget
  meeting.

  Commissioner Jennings stated that after the Woolsey Fire, Councilmember Peak
  suggested adding a process to make it easier to rebuild or make additions,
  including basements, and noted that it is not viable to add a basement after
  construction.

  Chair Hill asked for clarification on the context for determining whether a project
  is considered complete or not. In response to John Johanessen, he noted
  Commissioners are interested in the Malibu Film Society and would like it to
  progress. He added that the Planning Commission does not have an item
  schedu led on that topic.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of April 18, 2022
  Page 3 of 8

Chair Hill asked for clarification on whether the current Malibu barber pole
matches what was approved by the Planning Commission, and if not, the process
to bring it into compliance.

Chair Hill stated hybrid meetings would provide consistency during COVID, as it
appeared likely to continue for the near future. In cases where he chose to abstain
from the vote, it was because he did not have enough information to make a
reasoned decision on the matter.

Commissioner Mazza stated he viewed the staff report and the wireless tower by
the community college building was not proposed as red and white. He noted the
County of Los Angeles recommended wearing masks and testing before and after
face-to-face meetings.

Commissioner Jennings agreed that hybrid meetings would be a good idea and
suggested that staff should be able to participate remotely as well, possibly
lowering compensation time expenses.

Planning Director Mollica noted the Department had not previously received
complaints regarding the Malibu Jewish Center and Malibu Film Society
screenings so their schedule and locations were not tracked. He explained that the
Department has lacked staff and funding to follow community events advertised
in local papers and websites to verify whether they were permitted since 2007 and
when a complaint regarding Malibu Film Society events at the Malibu Jewish
Center was received, staff reviewed the conditional use permit. He added that the
Malibu Film Society can hold events within spaces where the venue is eligible to
host such events based on each site’s conditional use permit.

In response to Commissioner Mazza’s concerns about the wireless tower,
Planning Director Mollica noted this was part of the project approval replacing a
pre-existing 70-foot tower in the same location as the old and it was approved as a
tower with marker lights on it. He stated that the prior tower’s colors were
aviation orange and white, though the colors had faded over time. He added that
due to proximity to the sheriffs helipad, the colors and lights may be a required
federal aviation safety issue. He informed the Commission that staff will verify
that the installation is correctly located.

In response to Jo Drummond, Planning Director Mollica noted there are two
separate sections of code she referenced, one about exemptions and applications
and the other about stringlines. He stated the prior Planning Director discussed
exemptions both internally and with the California Coastal Commission to set
guidelines and create a practice to follow, which was vetted through two City
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes of April 18, 2022
  Page 4 of 8

  Council public hearings. He added that these prior policies are reversible should
  the City Council so choose.
